corrected_value.authors: Bönte, W., Procher, V. D., & Urbig, D.
corrected_value.title: Biology and selection into entrepreneurship: The relevance of prenatal testosterone exposure.

decisions.quote: Fourth, in order to replicate Nicolaou et al. (2018), we define the dependent variable, the control variables, and the sample as closely to this study as possible. Our failure to find significant effects does not rule out that 2D:4D is associated with other outcomes related to entrepreneurship such as entrepreneurial intent, as reported by Bönte et al. (2016) for university students; however, it is unclear in how far entrepreneurial intent among students will materialize in actual entrepreneurial behavior later in life. It is also possible that biological factors, including 2D:4D, affect younger persons more than older persons, who have been subject to more intervening nonbiological influences (Bönte et al., 2017). In an additional not preregistered exploratory analysis, we test for an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in our data using a measure of entrepreneurial intent similar to one of the measures used by Bönte et al. (2016). We find no statistically significant or suggestive evidence of an association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent in this analysis.
decisions.reason: The shipped original (Manning, Kilduff, & Trivers, 2013 [online 2012], DOI 10.1111/j.2047-2927.2012.00013.x) is cited only once in the Discussion as background literature on 2D:4D in men with Klinefelter's syndrome and is never re-tested. Beyond the primary replication of Nicolaou et al. (2018) (paired with shipped row 1250 / target 0), the paper conducts an empirical new-sample retest of the association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent reported by Bönte, Procher, & Urbig (2016) (as well as their age-moderation claim) using SOEP-IS data, so blind target 1 is the actual tested original for this row.

decisions.reason: Both the paper as a whole and the specific retest of Bönte et al. (2016) use newly collected 2D:4D data and survey responses from the German Socioeconomic Panel-Innovation Sample (SOEP-IS) to test a previously published finding in an independent sample, which is a replication.

decisions.reason: Evaluating the outcome for the resolved tested original Bönte et al. (2016) (whereas the shipped row's quote concerned self-employment for the misidentified original): the Introduction and Results note that Bönte et al. (2016) reported significant negative associations between right-hand 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent among university students and argued the effect is stronger in younger individuals, whereas this paper's corresponding SOEP-IS regressions find no statistically significant or suggestive association between 2D:4D and entrepreneurial intent and no interaction with age. Parent consistency inspection: this independently source-supported outcome value exactly equals the actual shipped outcome. Only the verdict flag is corrected to shipped_right; the earlier blind_right flag is inconsistent and was rejected by the existing comparison guard. No scientific value, quote, target allocation or raw expert reply changes. This flag correction does not itself resolve any separately pending original-identity dependency.
